title: Chest Pain

rationale.Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular: BP in both arms — differential >20mmHg. Aortic regurgitation murmur. Pulse deficit.
rationale.CT angiography chest/abd/pelvis: Diagnostic. Identifies dissection flap, extent, branch involvement.
rationale.ECG: Rule out MI. May show LVH from HTN.
rationale.IV beta-blocker (Esmolol): First: reduce HR/dP/dt. Then vasodilator. Target HR 60, SBP 100-120.
rationale.Cardiothoracic surgery consult: Type A = surgical emergency. OR now.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset severe tearing/ripping chest pain radiating to the back between the scapulae. Pain is maximal at onset (unlike MI which builds). Exam reveals differential BP between arms (>20mmHg), pulse deficit, new aortic regurgitation murmur. May have neurologic deficits if dissection involves carotid arteries. Risk factors: hypertension (most common), connective tissue disorders (Marfan, Ehlers-Danlos), bicuspid aortic valve, cocaine, pregnancy. CXR shows widened mediastinum (>8cm). CT angiography of chest/abdomen/pelvis is diagnostic. TEE can be done at bedside. Stanford type A (ascending aorta) = SURGICAL EMERGENCY. Stanford type B (descending aorta only) = medical management (BP control). Start IV beta-blocker (esmolol first — lowers dP/dt) then add vasodilator (nitroprusside or nicardipine). Target HR 60 and SBP 100-120. Consult cardiothoracic surgery immediately.
